hello.note: Reply: wa alaikum assalam (وعلیکم السلام). Very Pashto: stari ma shai (ستړي مه شئ), 'may you not be tired'.

goodbye.note: The one staying behind often replies: pa makha de sha (په مخه دې ښه), 'safe journey'.

please.note: Literally 'do a kindness'. Also very common: lutfan (لطفاً).

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: dera manana (ډېره مننه). Also common: tashakor (تشکر).

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'it's nothing'. Also: khair dey (خیر دی).

sorry.note: ښ sounds sh in the south, kh in the east (bakhkhana). Also: mazerat ghwaram (معذرت غواړم).

good_morning.note: Mo (مو) is the polite 'your'. To a friend: sahar de pa khair (سهار دې په خیر).

how_are_you.note: To a friend: ta tsanga ye? (ته څنګه یې؟)

im_fine.note: Very common: shukar, sha yam (شکر، ښه یم), 'thank God, I'm fine'.

whats_your_name.note: To a friend or child: sta noom tsa dey? (ستا نوم څه دی؟)

nice_to_meet_you.note: Literally 'I am glad to have seen you'. Same words for men and women.

where_from.note: To a friend: ta da kom dzay ye? (ته د کوم ځای یې؟)

im_from.note: Literally 'I am of …', e.g. za da Kanada yam (زه د کاناډا یم).

speak_english.note: In Pakistan English is usually angrezi (انګرېزي).

dont_understand.note: ږ is zh in the south, g in the east (pohegam). Also: poh na shwam (پوه نه شوم), 'I didn't get it'.

how_much.note: Also: qimat ye tso dey? (قیمت یې څو دی؟), 'what's its price?'

can_you_help.text: تاسو زما سره مرسته کولای شئ؟
can_you_help.roman: Taso zama sara mrasta kawalay shai?

one.note: Before a feminine noun: yawa (یوه). Digit: ۱

water.note: Always plural in grammar: oba sare di (اوبه سړې دي), 'the water is cold'.

coffee.note: In Pakistan qahwa usually means green tea; coffee there is kafi (کافي).

tea.note: Green tea: shin chay (شین چای). Black tea: tor chay (تور چای).

bread.note: Also means 'food' or 'a meal' in general.

im_hungry.note: A woman says: za wazhe yam (زه وږې یم).

enjoy_meal.note: Said to someone eating, and the usual reply when a guest thanks you for the food.

left.note: Literally 'to the left hand'. Many also say chap (چپ).

right.note: Literally 'to the right hand'. In the east ښ is kh: khi las ta.

straight_ahead.note: Go straight ahead: makhamakh lar shai (مخامخ لاړ شئ).

airport.note: In Kabul many also say the Dari maidan-e hawayi (میدان هوایی).

hotel.note: Also used for a simple restaurant or roadside eatery.

too_expensive.note: To haggle: lazh ye kam krai (لږ یې کم کړئ), 'bring it down a bit'.

id_like_this.note: Literally 'please give me this'. Also: za da ghwaram (زه دا غواړم), 'I want this'.

just_looking.note: Also: hamdase goram (همداسې ګورم). Yawaze goram (یوازې ګورم) is understood but sounds literal.

open.note: In speech: khlas dey (خلاص دی), 'it's open'.

closed.note: In speech: band dey (بند دی), 'it's closed'.

big.note: Feminine: loya (لویه), as in Loya Jirga.

see_you_later.note: Literally 'we will see each other again'.

wait_moment.note: Casual: lazh sabar wukra (لږ صبر وکړه).

help.note: You can also just shout mrasta! (مرسته!)

need_doctor.note: Colloquial: daktar me pa kar dey (ډاکټر مې په کار دی).

im_lost.note: Literally 'I have lost my way'. Same for men and women.

be_careful.note: To a friend or child: pam kawa! (پام کوه!)

no_problem.note: Literally 'it doesn't matter'. Also: koma khabara na da (کومه خبره نه ده).

dont_know.note: A woman says: khabara na yam (خبره نه یم). Na pohezham (نه پوهېږم) also works.

i_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: khwasha me da (خوښه مې ده).

dont_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: khwasha me na da (خوښه مې نه ده).

im_tired.note: A woman says: za stare yam (زه ستړې یم).

im_happy.note: Same form for men and women.

welcome.note: Formal, and on signs: sha raghlast (ښه راغلاست).

brother.note: Plural: wruna (وروڼه). An elder brother is often called lala (لالا).

child.note: A girl: bachai (بچۍ). Also: zoy (زوی), 'son', and lur (لور), 'daughter'.

friend.note: A female friend: malgare (ملګرې). Also very common: dost (دوست).

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: da zama malgare da (دا زما ملګرې ده).

are_you_married.note: Reply: ho, wada me karay dey (هو، واده مې کړی دی), 'yes, I'm married'.

have_children.note: Often asked as: tso bachi larai? (څو بچي لرئ؟), 'how many children do you have?'

wednesday.note: Spelled with چهار but usually said charshanba.

weekend.note: Literally 'the end of the week'. Also: da onai rukhsati (د اونۍ رخصتي).

what_day.note: Also: nan koma wradz da? (نن کومه ورځ ده؟)

twenty.note: In 21–29 it becomes wisht: yawwisht (یوویشت), 21. Digits: ۲۰

hundred.note: Two hundred: dwa sawa (دوه سوه). Digits: ۱۰۰

thousand.note: Two thousand: dwa zara (دوه زره). Digits: ۱۰۰۰

how_old.note: To a friend or child: ta tso kalan ye? (ته څو کلن یې؟)

years_old.note: A woman says: za … kalana yam (زه … کلنه یم).

blue.note: Same for both genders. Shin (شین) can mean blue or green; abi is clearly blue.

another_one.text: مهرباني وکړئ، یو بل هم راکړئ
another_one.roman: Mehrabani wukrai, yaw bal ham rakrai
another_one.note: For a feminine item: yawa bala (یوه بله).

its_hot.note: Also: hawa garma da (هوا ګرمه ده), 'the weather is hot'.

its_cold.note: Also: hawa sara da (هوا سړه ده), 'the weather is cold'.

its_sunny.note: Literally 'the sun is out'. Also: hawa safa da (هوا صافه ده), 'the sky is clear'.

its_windy.note: Literally 'wind is blowing'. Casual: der bad dey (ډېر باد دی), 'it's very windy'.

beautiful_day.note: Also: nan hawa dera sha da (نن هوا ډېره ښه ده), 'the weather is lovely today'.

have_reservation.note: Literally 'I have reserved a room'. Also: ma makhke kota niwale da (ما مخکې کوټه نیولې ده).

wifi_password.text: د وای فای پاسورډ څه دی؟
wifi_password.roman: Da wai fai pasward tsa dey?

check_out_time.text: کوټه باید څو بجې خالي کړم؟
check_out_time.roman: Kota bayad tso baje khali kram?
check_out_time.note: Literally 'what time must I vacate the room?'

is_this_seat_free.note: Also: dalta tsok nast dey? (دلته څوک ناست دی؟), 'is anyone sitting here?'

what_do_you_do.note: Also: staso danda tsa da? (ستاسو دنده څه ده؟), 'what's your job?'

i_work_in.note: E.g. za pa bank ke kar kawam (زه په بانک کې کار کوم).

im_student.note: A woman says: za muhassila yam (زه محصله یم). A school pupil: zda kawunkay (زده کوونکی).

im_busy.note: A woman says: za bukhta yam (زه بوخته یم).

day_off.note: 'I'm off today': nan rukhsat yam (نن رخصت یم).

lets_start.note: Casual: shuru ye kro (شروع یې کړو).

good_job.note: Also: der sha kar mo karay dey (ډېر ښه کار مو کړی دی), 'you've done great work'.

table_for_two.text: مهرباني وکړئ، د دوو کسانو لپاره مېز
table_for_two.roman: Mehrabani wukrai, da dwo kasano lpara mez

what_recommend.text: ستاسو په نظر څه ښه دي؟
what_recommend.roman: Staso pa nazar tsa sha di?
what_recommend.note: Literally 'in your view, what's good?' Also: staso khas khwarak tsa dey? (ستاسو خاص خوراک څه دی؟)

not_spicy.text: مهرباني وکړئ، مرچ پکې مه اچوئ
not_spicy.roman: Mehrabani wukrai, mrach pake ma achawai
not_spicy.note: Literally 'please don't put chilli in it'.

no_sugar.text: مهرباني وکړئ، بوره پکې مه اچوئ
no_sugar.roman: Mehrabani wukrai, bura pake ma achawai
no_sugar.note: Literally 'please don't put sugar in it'. Sugar lumps: qand (قند).

im_full.note: A woman says: mara shwam (مړه شوم). To decline more politely: bas dey, manana (بس دی، مننه).

takeaway.text: مهرباني وکړئ، دا راته بسته کړئ
takeaway.roman: Mehrabani wukrai, da rata basta krai
takeaway.note: Literally 'please pack this for me'. In Pakistan people say parsal (پارسل).

it_was_delicious.note: For a feminine noun like dodai: dera khwandawara wa (ډېره خوندوره وه).

keep_change.note: Shorter: pate ye staso (پاتې یې ستاسو), 'the rest is yours'.

head_hurts.note: Also: sar me khwazhezhi (سر مې خوږېږي).

have_fever.note: Also: taba me da (تبه مې ده).

need_rest.note: Also: istirahat ta artya laram (استراحت ته اړتیا لرم).

feel_better.note: Also: os sha yam (اوس ښه یم), 'I'm fine now'.

get_well.note: Literally 'may God heal you'. Also: zhar jor shai! (ژر جوړ شئ!)

lets_meet.note: To one friend: radza (راځه) instead of radzai.

are_you_free.note: To a woman: taso saba wazgare yast? (تاسو سبا وزګارې یاست؟)

call_me.note: To a friend: rata zang wuwaha (راته زنګ ووهه).

your_number.text: ستاسو د تلیفون شمېره څه ده؟
your_number.roman: Staso da telefoon shmera tsa da?
your_number.note: Casual: nambar mo tsa dey? (نمبر مو څه دی؟)

have_nice_day.note: To a friend: wradz de sha tera shi! (ورځ دې ښه تېره شي!)

good_luck.note: To a woman: baryalai osai (بریالۍ اوسئ). Also: khuday de mal sha (خدای دې مل شه).

happy_birthday.text: د زوکړې ورځ مو مبارک شه!
happy_birthday.roman: Da zokre wradz mo mubarak sha!
happy_birthday.note: To a friend: de (دې) instead of mo (مو).

miss_you.text: زړه مې درپسې تنګ شوی دی
miss_you.roman: Zra me darpase tang shaway dey
miss_you.note: Literally 'my heart has grown tight for you'. Also: der rayadezhe (ډېر رایادېږې).
